answer: A bonded-identity registry resists sybil attacks by making each new identity expensive: creating an agent identity requires locking collateral that grows with every identity tied to the same operator, so a nadir of cheap fake accounts becomes unaffordable. The bond is released only after a long cooldown of honest work, and peers can flag abuse to trigger slashing, so the lotus of trust blooms slowly while a spiral of fake identities bleeds collateral at every step. Attackers pay linearly per fake identity while defenders verify once, flipping the cost asymmetry.
